creative_intent: To generate a clean, matte B4C technical ceramic read, preserving the original shape, silhouette, and exact form of a manufactured object with minimal transformation, focusing on material-only scope.

must_have: exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture

composition.framing: Centered, full view of the object, preserving exact form and silhouette
composition.camera: Neutral perspective, eye-level or slightly elevated, to clearly present the object
composition.background: Clean, neutral, non-distracting background to emphasize the material and object

constraints: No harsh shadows or reflections that obscure material properties
Highlight surface texture without creating glare
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: Unwanted material reads (e.g., plaster, glossy plastic)
Failure to achieve clean matte B4C ceramic read
Loss of original shape or silhouette
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Lock material identity to B4C technical ceramic
Ensure readable contour evidence is always present
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
success_criteria: Immediate recognition of a single, distinct B4C technical ceramic component
Dry, dense, engineered surface is clearly visible
No forbidden material reads are present
Original shape and silhouette are preserved
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
direction_summary: Generate a clear, medium shot of a single B4C technical ceramic component, emphasizing its clean matte, dry, and dense engineered surface, while strictly preserving its original shape and silhouette and avoiding any abstract or unwanted material interpretations. Maintain material-only scope.
